holding_summary: An unlicensed keeper of a boarding house and tavern (the United States Hotel) may recover in assumpsit for boarding and lodging furnished to a guest and his family over roughly six months, notwithstanding the same guest was also furnished liquor without a license during the period, because the boarding claim is severable from the illegal liquor claim and boardinghouse-keeping is a distinct lawful pursuit from innkeeping.

quotes.text: The keeper of a boarding-house may recover his claim for boarding a person and his family, though during the same period of time he furnished the said individual with liquor, for which the former had an account; the said boarding-house keeper, during the same time, not having any license to sell liquor.
The employment of the former is to furnish subsistence and lodging to permanent residents; of the taverner, to entertain temporary guests.
he also practised the lawful business of a boardinghouse keeper, which could not be rendered illegal by the fact that transient guests were received and entertained in the same house.

holding_summary: A boarder's furniture kept in his rooms at a boarding house is exempt from distress for the rent owed by the boarding-house keeper to her landlord, because the public-convenience privilege that protects a guest's goods at an inn extends to a lodger's effects at a boarding house, even though the boarder is not a technical undertenant.

quotes.text: The goods of a boarder are not liable to be distrained for rent due by the keeper of the boarding-house.

In the next, he has no term or interest in the place; for though a chamber is incidentally assigned to him among the appliances of the tenant’s business, he has no' other title to it than he has to the plate off which he eats, or the chair on which he sits at table : it is his while he uses it, but another’s the moment he relinquishes it.
The keeping of a boarding and lodging house, is as distinctly a public profession here, as is that of a warehouse-man or wharfinger in England; and it necessarily has the same incidents.

notes: Duration of Riddle's occupancy as a boarder is not stated; the opinion addresses the legal status of lodgers generally rather than the facts of this particular boarder's stay.

Dispute over a parol lease/license to dig ore from a mine-bank on defendant's land; general lease-vs-license-at-will language was retrieved but the case does not involve letting a dwelling or rooms for occupancy.

Concerns whether a licensed innkeeper's Sunday liquor sale to a 'sojourner' violates the 1794 Sunday-labor statute and the interplay with the 1834 tavern-licensing acts; touches inn licensing only as to liquor sales, not the right to let rooms or dwellings for pay.

Farm lease/distress-for-rent dispute involving livestock and a lease of realty with personal property; 'ready furnished lodgings' is mentioned only once, in dicta, as an analogy for rent issuing out of land, not as a lodging-letting case itself.

Church-trustee quo warranto/writ-of-assistance dispute; leases of the pastor's residence and school-house rooms to individual occupants are held void as ultra vires acts of usurping trustees and as purchases pendente lite, not on any doctrine of lodging or short-term letting.
Industrial lease (forge, furnace, saw-mills) with rent payable in bar-iron; dispute over assignment of the lease and right to distrain. No residential letting or lodging is involved.

Procedural landlord-tenant dispute over whether a waiver of the statutory three-months' notice to quit must be found by the inquest; the underlying one-year lease is not shown to involve lodging or boarding.

County commissioners leased a house as a residence for the sheriff and his family; the dispute is about the county's liability for rent under an implied holding-over lease, not about the practice of letting rooms or dwellings to boarders/lodgers.
County commissioners leased a vacant jail-adjacent lot to a private party for a marble manufactory; dispute concerns distribution of distress/execution proceeds, not residential letting or lodging.

Habeas corpus proceeding testing whether a licensed innkeeper's Sunday liquor sale is indictable as a tippling-house offense; discusses the inn-licensing scheme but only as to liquor sales, not the right to let rooms or dwellings for pay.
Trespass quare clausum fregit over a farm lease; holds a landlord who parted with entire possession cannot maintain the action. No lodging or boarding facts.
Commercial store lease and holdover-tenancy rule (use and occupation); no residential lodging or boarding is at issue.
Demise at will of church premises in consideration of services as foresinger/organist; a landlord-and-tenant-act procedure case with no lodging or boarding facts.
Ground-rent conveyance and assignee-indemnity dispute over an urban lot; no lodging, boarding, or short-term occupancy facts.
Ground-rent covenant dispute over a wharf lot and riparian wharfing rights below low-water-mark; no lodging or boarding facts.
Farm crop-share lease dispute (hay division) and landlord eviction/trespass doctrine; no lodging or boarding facts.
Party-wall cost-reimbursement dispute between adjoining owners; the right is held personal to the original builder and not appurtenant to the land. No lodging or boarding facts.
